bib.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed., Chapter 15: Neuroscience

question: What parallels exist between reinforcement learning algorithms (TD error, actor-critic, eligibility traces) and the neural basis of reward-based learning in animals?
hypothesis: The reward prediction error hypothesis: phasic dopamine neuron activity conveys TD errors, and the brain may implement something like an actor-critic algorithm.
contributions: Explains the reward prediction error hypothesis of dopamine neuron activity and the experiments behind it
Maps actor-critic with eligibility traces onto striatal circuitry and reward-modulated STDP
Presents Klopf's hedonistic neuron and collective (team) reinforcement learning with REINFORCE units
Outlines model-based methods in the brain and a TD model of addiction

results.claim: Phasic dopamine responses correspond to the TD error delta_{t-1}, not to the reward R_t.
results.setup: Reward prediction error hypothesis, Schultz-lab recordings in monkeys vs TD model with CSC representation
results.quote: phasic responses of dopamine neurons signal reward prediction errors, not reward itself.

results.claim: TD error available at t, used as the reinforcement signal.
results.setup: TD error delta_{t-1} = R_t + gamma V(S_t) - V(S_{t-1})
results.quote: the reinforcement signal at time t is the TD error δt−1 = Rt + γV (St) −V (St−1).

results.claim: Idealised TD(0) policy-evaluation trace: at the unpredicted reward delta equals R*; after learning delta is zero at reward and positive at the earliest predictor; on omission delta = -R*.
results.setup: Tabular TD(0), V initialised to zero, CSC representation, deterministic task, gamma near 1, predictions confined to a trial (Fig 15.4)
results.quote: the TD error goes negative at the usual time of reward because the value of the latest reward-predicting state is then too high

results.claim: Hollerman and Schultz (1998): reward arriving earlier than expected does not produce the sub-baseline dopamine dip that the CSC TD model predicts.
results.setup: Dopamine recordings vs TD with CSC representation
results.quote: dopamine neuron activity does not drop below baseline in the way the TD model predicts (Hollerman and Schultz, 1998)

results.claim: Actor-critic with eligibility traces: critic uses non-contingent trace, actor uses contingent trace; the only difference between the two learning rules.

results.claim: Reward-modulated STDP at corticostriatal synapses: lasting change occurs only if a neuromodulator pulse arrives within a window lasting up to 10 seconds.
results.setup: Corticostriatal synapses of medium spiny neurons
results.quote: within a time window that can last up to 10 seconds after a presynaptic spike is closely followed by a postsynaptic spike

limits: Authors say they are not neuroscientists and the chapter is too short to cover the brain structures, pathways and molecular mechanisms (p.379).
Alternative hypotheses are not treated; O'Reilly and Frank argue dopamine signals RPEs but not TD errors (p.413).
Discrepancies remain, notably early-reward timing; CSC representation is a modelling choice that matters (p.393-394).

Dopamine neurons are probably not a single broadcast scalar; subpopulations differ (p.385). The actor-critic mapping to dorsal/ventral striatum is acknowledged as too simple given DLS/DMS results (p.407).
The model-free actor-critic covers only habitual behaviour (p.407). Addiction model is partial (p.410).
Chapter is from 2018 and neuroscience findings cited stop around 2016.
practices: Distinguish the reward signal R_t from the reinforcement signal (TD error), which drives learning in most algorithms (p.380).
Use the TD error as the shared reinforcement signal for both actor and critic; it differs only in the eligibility trace each uses (p.395, 400).
Use contingent eligibility traces (grad ln pi) for control and non-contingent traces for prediction (p.406).
Maintain action variability so a team of agents explores the collective action space (p.406).
A broadcast scalar reinforcement signal can train a multilayer network via REINFORCE, as a slower but neurally plausible alternative to backprop (p.407).

terms.definition: one of the functions of the phasic activity of dopamine-producing neurons in mammals is to deliver an error between an old and a new estimate of expected future reward to target areas throughout the brain
directs the changes a learning algorithm makes in an agent's policy, value estimates, or environment models; for TD methods it is the TD error
a trace initiated or increased at a synapse when presynaptic input participates in causing the postsynaptic neuron to fire (depends on the unit's output)
a trace initiated or increased by presynaptic input independently of what the postsynaptic neuron does
learning rule in which a reinforcement signal interacts with eligibility traces depending on both presynaptic and postsynaptic activity (actor rule); the critic rule is two-factor
spike-timing-dependent plasticity where changes also require a neuromodulator such as dopamine within a time window after the pre/post spike pairing
all agents try to maximize a common reward signal they simultaneously receive
which team members, or groups, deserve credit for a favorable reward signal or blame for an unfavorable one
Klopf's conjecture that individual neurons seek to maximize the difference between synaptic input treated as rewarding and as punishing
state representation with a distinct internal signal for each time step following a stimulus
Selfridge's strategy: keep going in the same way if things are getting better, and otherwise move around
